name: Terraform
summary: A declarative infrastructure tool that builds a dependency graph from configuration, providers, and state, then plans and applies changes toward the declared resource configuration.

features.name: Declarative resource dependency graph
features.description: Terraform translates configuration into resource nodes and dependency edges, using references and explicit dependencies to determine an order for planning and applying changes.
benefits: Makes dependency ordering explicit and repeatable
Allows a configuration to describe desired infrastructure rather than imperative steps
costs: Implicit dependencies can be difficult to inspect
Cycles or incomplete dependencies prevent a valid execution order

features.name: Provider and resource boundary
features.description: Terraform delegates resource and data-source behavior to providers through a provider boundary, allowing the core graph and lifecycle engine to coordinate resources without implementing every external API.
benefits: Extends Terraform to many infrastructure APIs
Separates graph orchestration from provider-specific resource operations
costs: Provider schemas and behavior become part of the configuration contract
External API and provider version differences affect plans

features.name: Plan, apply, and state lifecycle
features.description: Terraform compares configuration, prior state, and provider observations to produce a plan, then applies the selected changes and records resulting resource state for later reconciliation.
benefits: Provides a reviewable intermediate plan before mutation
Retains resource identity and observed attributes across runs
costs: State must be protected, synchronized, and kept compatible with providers
External drift and unknown values complicate planning

mathematical_views.question: When does a configured set of resources admit a valid topological order for planning and application?
assumptions: Nodes represent resource and data operations
Provider side effects are abstracted behind node operations

mathematical_views.question: How can configuration, prior state, and provider observations determine a proposed resource transition?
assumptions: Provider reads and plans expose sufficiently comparable values
Unknown and sensitive values follow Terraform's evaluation rules
The model abstracts remote API transaction semantics

mathematical_views.question: Which resource operations can be composed into one graph while preserving provider schema and lifecycle contracts?
assumptions: Each provider implements the supported plugin contract
Resource schemas define valid configuration and state fields
Composition does not imply atomicity across providers

benefits: Automatic dependency ordering and parallelizable work
costs: Graph construction and cycle diagnosis add conceptual complexity
Provider compatibility and API behavior affect reproducibility

benefits: Reviewable changes and persistent resource identity
costs: State security, locking, drift, and unknown values require operations discipline
